predecessors.name: Russian Eastern Outskirts
predecessors.text: Semyonov's Eastern Okraina at Chita, expelled in October 1920

successors.name: Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic
successors.text: the four provinces of the former Russian empire (Trans-Baikal, Amur, Maritime Province, northern Sakhalin), without the northern half of Sakhalin, which stayed under Japanese occupation until 1925

successors.name: Provisional Priamurye Government
successors.text: the Vladivostok enclave, which the infobox lists among the successor states

ledger.x: 1920, 6 April: a hastily convened Constituent Assembly at Verkhneudinsk proclaims the Far Eastern Republic, a buffer state between Soviet Russia and Japan; at first it comprises "only the area around Verkhneudinsk".
1920, summer: the Soviet government of the Amur territory agrees to join; on 15 July 1920 Japan agrees in a truce with the Red Army to recognise the new buffer state.

1920, 19 October: Red forces of the FER begin advancing on Chita after the Japanese left it on 15 October; Semyonov had passed his civil powers to a Provisional Eastern-Transbaikal Assembly in September.
1920, 22 October: Chita falls to the Red forces; Semyonov's regime, "left without territory, collapsed" and the FER takes Transbaikal and moves its capital to Chita.
1920, 22 October: fighting for Chita ends with its capture.
1920, October: the capital moves from Verkhneudinsk to Chita.

1920: the republic that "was established comprising only the area around Verkhneudinsk" in April is by the 1921 keyframe the whole of Buryatia, Transbaikal and Amur: the page says it "consisted of four provinces...
1920, November: the Maritime Province enters the FER on paper.
1921-1922: the Priamur enclave "was gradually expanded to Khabarovsk and then to Spassk".
1921: bridge to the 1921 keyframe (Buryatia, Transbaikal and Amur only).
1921, 23-27 May: a White coup by the Kappelevtsy and the Merkulov brothers takes Vladivostok "to break away from the Far Eastern Republic"; the Provisional Priamurye…

1922, 25 October: "The army of the Far Eastern Republic retook Vladivostok"; the Japanese had announced on 24 June 1922 that they would remove all troops from Siberia by the end of October, and the FER "retook most of the Priamurye Government territory".
1922, 15 November: "With the Civil War finally over, Soviet Russia absorbed the Far Eastern Republic."
1922, 15 November: the Far Eastern Republic is dissolved into the Russian SFSR; northern Sakhalin remained under Japanese occupation until 1925.

wars.name: Siberian intervention
wars.outcome: The Japanese evacuated Transbaikal in 1920 (Gongota Agreement, Semyonov ended October 1920) and the rest of Siberia in October 1922; northern Sakhalin stayed occupied to 1925.

wars.name: Russian Civil War in the Far East (FER front)
wars.outcome: FER troops took Chita on 22 October 1920 and Vladivostok on 25 October 1922; the Japanese left in October 1922.

certainty.note: No treaty line: the frontier "followed the western coastline of Lake Baikal along the northern borders of Mongolia and Manchuria"; the Japanese cordon around Vladivostok is a military line, not a border.
